quotes.text: A confidence score is a value from 0 to 1 that quantifies doubt. It is the models way of saying, "I think this is a match, and here is how much I'm willing to bet on it."
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a crisp, memorable definition of confidence scores as the basis of probabilistic design.

quotes.text: There is one fundamental rule for the modern architect. Never let a large language model do the math. LLMs are engines for soft reasoning, which makes them great at understanding intent or finding a specific detail in a pile of messy text.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States a clear architectural rule for separating LLM reasoning from deterministic calculation.

quotes.text: You do not trust the model, you trust the architecture you built around it. You create a safety net so strong that the occasional stumble from the model does not even count as an error.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the self-correcting workflow idea in one quotable principle.

quotes.text: Successful designs in 2026 will treat verification work as a primary feature. They do not see human review as a failure of the system. Instead, they see it as a necessary part of the architecture.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes human review as a designed feature rather than a weakness of automation.

chapters.title: Confidence scores and the green, yellow and red zones
Implementation challenge: add a confidence threshold

takeaways: Deterministic if-then logic fails on messy, unstructured data, so modern Power Platform designs should route work by confidence score instead of exact matches.
Use the LLM for soft reasoning such as extraction, but let deterministic flows or rules engines do the math so hallucinations are caught and recovered from.
Treat human review as a designed tier for low-confidence cases, showing reviewers the source, the extraction and the weak field side by side.
hook: Your Power Automate flows keep breaking because they expect perfect data in a world full of typos, PDFs and chat messages. This episode is for Power Platform makers and architects who want to move from brittle if-then logic to probabilistic design with confidence scores, fuzzy matching and self-correcting workflows that survive real enterprise data.
